subject: Number of threads available of running INLA on HPC

messages.author: 7a4699cffe0ec852
messages.subject: Number of threads available of running INLA on HPC
parts:
Hello: everyone

I am running my INLA on a HPC, but It can only run on two threads.

res<- inla(formula,
           data = inla.stack.data(sdat),
            family="gaussian",
            control.compute = list(dic = TRUE, waic = TRUE, config = TRUE,return.marginals.predictor = TRUE),
             control.predictor = list(compute = TRUE,A = inla.stack.A(sdat)),
             control.fixed = list(mean.intercept=0,mean=0))

Warning message:
package ‘INLA’ was built under R version 4.2.2


You ask for 80 x 1 = 80 number of threads,
which is more that I got from the system: 2
Number of threads is reduced to 2:1



You ask for 80 x 1 = 80 number of threads,
which is more that I got from the system: 2
Number of threads is reduced to 2:1

From HPC support  " If you submit your job and run on a compute node, you can request up to 256 threads.  Your code may not be able to effectively use 256 threads"

How can I get it to run on more threads? It has been running for more than 10 hours without crashing or ending. And by the way, is inla.pardiso() can be used?

Kind regards
You

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Number of threads available of running INLA on HPC
parts:
Hi,

I guess this is not influenced by the warning ``package ‘INLA’ was built
under R version 4.2.2''. Which version of INLA and R are you using?


the code is using standard system calls to get the number of threads
available,


int host_max_threads = IMAX(omp_get_max_threads(), omp_get_num_procs());

so I do not know what is happening. You can try to do in R

> system(paste(INLA:::inla.call.builtin(),"-m openmp"))


which should return at the end,

export OMP_NUM_THREADS=8,1,1,1; export OMP_NESTED=TRUE; export
OMP_MAX_ACTIVE_LEVELS=8; >


meaning that there is 8 threads available.


please check and get back to me.

Best
H

good. there is a limit how many threads that can be used. without
PARDISO, then its basically number of hyperparameters x 2. in the
integration phase it can use more. in the optimisation phase it can use
more, if you enable nested parallel, ie num.threads="8:2", f.ex.

this paper
